extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset v1.0 (SQuAD)
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset containing 107,785 question-answer pairs on 536 English Wikipedia articles. Questions were posed by crowdworkers, and each answer is a text span from the corresponding passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, and Percy Liang
extraction.citeAs: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, and Percy Liang. SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. arXiv:1606.05250v3 [cs.CL], 11 October 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Collection proceeded in three stages: passage curation, crowdsourcing question-answer pairs, and obtaining additional answers. Using Project Nayuki's Wikipedia internal PageRanks, the authors identified the top 10,000 English Wikipedia articles and sampled 536 uniformly at random. Paragraph extraction and filtering yielded 23,215 paragraphs. Crowdworkers created up to five questions and highlighted their answers per paragraph. At least two additional answers were collected for each development and test question. Workers were paid $9 per hour, asked to spend four minutes per paragraph when creating questions, and recommended five questions per two minutes when providing additional answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During additional answer collection, workers were instructed to submit a question without marking an answer if it was not answerable by a span in the paragraph. In the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English Wikipedia articles selected from the top 10,000 articles ranked using Project Nayuki's Wikipedia internal PageRanks, together with questions and answer spans authored by crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The 536 sampled articles were randomly partitioned into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Individual paragraphs were extracted from the sampled articles. Images, figures, and tables were stripped away, and paragraphs shorter than 500 characters were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers entered up to five questions per paragraph in text fields and highlighted the corresponding answer spans. Tasks included a sample paragraph and examples of good and bad questions and answers with explanations. Workers were encouraged to use their own words rather than copy phrases; reminders appeared at the beginning of each paragraph, and copying and pasting paragraph text was disabled. Additional annotators saw the questions and paragraphs and selected the shortest answering span, leaving the answer unmarked when no span answered the question. For a separate reasoning analysis, the authors manually labeled 192 development examples with one or more reasoning categories.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo, with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend, and a crowd-facing web interface for entering questions and highlighting answer spans.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Development and test questions received multiple answers to make evaluation more robust and estimate human performance. Human evaluation treated the second answer as the prediction and the remaining answers as ground truth, producing test exact match of 77.0% and F1 of 86.8%. Mismatches mostly reflected inclusion or exclusion of non-essential phrases rather than fundamental disagreement. Model exact match accepted a match to any ground-truth answer; F1 used the maximum score over ground-truth answers. Both metrics ignored punctuation and articles. In the manually analyzed sample of 192 examples, 6.1% were categorized as ambiguous because the authors disagreed with the crowdworker answer or the question lacked a unique answer.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One original answer per question, with at least two additional answers per development and test question, yielding at least three answers for each development and test question.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers were required to be located in the United States or Canada, have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, and have completed at least 1,000 HITs.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP generated constituency parses and part-of-speech tags for automatic answer-type categorization; named-entity recognition tags were used to distinguish person, location, and other entities.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper describes SQuAD v1.0 and mentions v1.1. All experimental results in the paper use v1.0. No updating schedule, maintainer responsibilities, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Answers are constrained to spans in the corresponding passage, making the questions more constrained than interpretative questions in advanced standardized tests. Systems have access to a single passage rather than multiple supporting documents. Some questions were judged unanswerable by additional annotators, and the manual analysis identified ambiguous questions or disputed answers.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of reading comprehension and question-answering models that select answer spans from a provided passage. The dataset is intended to support research into more expressive models and natural language understanding. Evaluation uses exact match and macro-averaged token-overlap F1 against human-provided answers.
